 Punjab government hikes DA by 40% for 6,507 computer teachers
 Press Trust of India | November 8, 2026 | 01:03 PM IST | 1 min read
 The Punjab government has increased the dearness allowance for computer teachers from 181 percent to 221 percent and regularised the services of non-teaching staff under Samagra Shiksha.
 Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann announces DA hike. (Representative Image: Wikimedia Commons) CHANDIGARH: The Punjab government on Saturday announced a 40 per cent hike in dearness allowance (DA) for 6,507 computer teachers and regularised services for 1,007 non-teaching employees working under Samagra Shiksha.
"On the auspicious occasion of Diwali, the Punjab government has announced a major benefit for its employees. 
 The government has approved a historic 40 per cent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for 6,507 Computer Teachers (PICTES), taking it from 181 per cent to 221 per cent," Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said in a statement.
The state government has also regularised the services of 1,007 non-teaching employees working under Samagra Shiksha. This decision will provide greater stability and security to these employees, he added.

 The state government has also decided to extend salary-related benefits to these employees. The government is fully committed to the welfare of its employees and ensuring their secure future, Mann said.
"No stone is being left unturned by the state government to ensure the welfare and well-being of its employees. We are committed to providing them with a secure future and ensuring that they receive the benefits they deserve," he noted.
